answer: Treat an identity's first funding as a dye: every new account carries the pigment of whoever paid its join fee. When a tide of fresh accounts shares one pigment, their grades of each other count once, not many times, and their unsettled payouts wait in escrow. A farm can launder through intermediaries, but each hop costs a fee and an epoch, so the spiral of disguise gets slower and pricier with every identity added.
